current_formulation: Prompted and fine-tuned generative language models, where the prompt must be tuned per model and dataset (2023 to 2024).

steps.formulation: Probabilistic model with attribute similarities as comparison vectors (Fellegi and Sunter 1969), known through a survey.
steps.quote: The first probabilistic model for ER [63] used attribute similarities as the dimensions of comparison vectors

steps.formulation: Deep learning matchers (DeepER, DeepMatcher) with word embeddings and an architecture template, as the 2020 survey reports them.
steps.quote: DeepMatcher [122] extends DeepER by introducing an architecture template for deep learning ER methods

steps.formulation: Ditto: fine-tuned pre-trained language models as a sequence-pair classifier.
steps.quote: a straightforward application of language models such as BERT, DistilBERT, or RoBERTa pre-trained on large text corpora already significantly improves the matching quality

criticism.quote: the fine-tuned models are not robust concerning out-of-distribution entities

steps.formulation: Generative LLMs for matching, where the prompt must be tuned for each model and dataset.
steps.quote: there is no single best prompt but that the prompt needs to be tuned for each model/dataset combination
